text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures were firmer in late trade as the market traded in strong volumes while awaiting the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in the United States. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 98.19, up 0.31 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts held steady on Tuesday, reacting neither to rumours that Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke had resigned, nor to the Treasury's denial. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-15/32, up 03/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures tagged Bund futures on Tuesday during a lacklustre session with little domestic news to spark interest ahead of the outcome of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy meeting today. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 124.12 up 0.28 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets soared as inflation fears melted away and were displaced by a mood of growing confidence in the government's ability to fashion a convincing 1997 budget and win approval for it in parliament. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 119.24 up 0.53 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were little changed in thin midday trade as anxiety ahead of the outcome of a meeting of Federal Reserve policy makers Tuesday lingered on, analysts said. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-02/32, down 01/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.02 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures ended slightly firmer on Tuesday on light position adjustment ahead of a Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later in the day and a 10-year JGB auction planned on Wednesday. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.14, up 0.15 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was limited on Tuesday, with most players waiting to see whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) would raise U.S. interest rates at today's meeting. "There are few plans at the moment, it all depends on what happens in the U.S. Treasury market," said a syndicate head at a British bank. A survey by Reuters showed the majority of U.S. economists expected rates to rise by 25 basis points. A number of FRNs, the price of which is not so sensitive to changes in interest rates, did surface.
